goal: Provide deterministic, compact project continuity across AI work sessions.
decisions: Canonical current state is continuity/state.json
History is append-only continuity/events.jsonl
Integrity validation is a first-class command and must fail closed on malformed state or events.
Every push and pull request is intended to run unit tests plus continuity validation in GitHub Actions.
Machine-readable handoffs use canonical compact JSON without volatile timestamps and include up to five recent failures.
Schema v2 adds a monotonic revision counter; v1 remains readable but must be explicitly migrated before mutation.
Mutating commands accept --expect-revision and reject stale writers before state or event side effects.
Mutations use a durable transaction journal with idempotent recovery so interrupted state/event writes converge to one logical commit.
All recovery and mutation critical sections are serialized by a standard-library cross-platform interprocess advisory lock.
A standalone integrity verifier audits transaction checksums and optional event hash chains without mutating project state.
CI failures are recorded as evidence and fixed before claiming the feature verified.
Pre-checksum transaction journals remain readable; new checksum enforcement can be introduced without breaking existing state.
The integrity verifier must distinguish legacy-readable data from tampered protected data.
New transaction journals are checksummed at creation and recovery fails closed on checksum mismatch.
New event records emit an optional prev_hash/chain_hash link so append-only history can be tamper-evident while legacy events remain readable.
The integrity verifier exposes a non-mutating audit mode that reports the first broken event-chain link as machine-readable JSON.
Transaction-journal audit uses the same stable valid/checked/first_break schema and remains non-mutating.
A CI regression is not considered resolved until the corrected test suite reports success.
Aggregate audit output must report event and transaction diagnostics together while preserving legacy command behavior.
Regression fixtures must write the intended corrupted bytes before invoking an audit command; passing tests must exercise the claimed failure mode.
Integrity audit exit codes are documented: 0 for valid selected scope and 1 for malformed or tampered protected data.
A protected event chain must begin at GENESIS; orphaned first links are invalid even when their individual hash matches.
Audit diagnostics use schema version 1 and aggregate first_break selects the earliest available domain diagnostic without changing legacy exit codes.
CI run 35626854032 completed successfully for the versioned audit implementation and its regression suite.
Schema-versioned audit examples belong in README.md and must show deterministic valid and broken aggregate outputs without implying runtime verification.
Contract tests must lock the documented audit schema keys and serialization order before further audit changes.
CI run 35639287923 completed successfully for the contract-test implementation.
Protected event hash fields must be strings, and chain_hash must be exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters before link or digest validation.
Recovery-boundary regressions must prove malformed transaction journals fail closed without mutating canonical state or append-only history.
Transaction recovery and standalone auditing now validate txid, state, and event shapes before checksum or mutation, with stable field-specific diagnostics.
Protected transaction checksums must be strings and exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters before comparison; legacy journals without checksums remain readable.
Standalone integrity auditing must reject non-object event records and non-object transaction journals with deterministic diagnostics instead of uncaught type errors.
Legacy transaction journals without checksums must still pass through the same required-shape validation before being accepted as readable.
continuity.py validate now invokes the non-mutating aggregate integrity audit and fails closed with a stable scope/line/reason diagnostic before reporting VALID.
Structured validation belongs in a separate non-mutating JSON entrypoint so machine consumers get stable diagnostics without changing the human-readable validate contract.
Structured validation must accept an explicit project root and rebind continuity paths before recovery or audit so tests and callers cannot accidentally validate the checkout containing the script.
Structured validation must read event records through the configured root after rebinding; imported path constants must not bypass explicit-root isolation.
Structured JSON validation must remain non-mutating: pending transaction journals are validated and reported, never recovered or deleted by the validator.
Read-only handoff must not recover or delete a pending transaction journal; it fails closed with a stable message until a mutating path completes recovery.
Read-only event readers must not call recovery implicitly; recovery is reserved for explicit mutating or recovery paths.
Explicit-root read-only snapshots must expose state and event metadata without recovery, deletion, or other file mutation, while reporting pending transactions deterministically.
Read-only snapshot failures must return a stable schema-versioned error object instead of exposing traceback-dependent exceptions.
continuity.py validate must not recover pending transaction journals implicitly; validation is read-only and reports a stable pending-journal diagnostic while preserving all canonical files.
Structured JSON validation reports pending transaction presence and txid explicitly while preserving the legacy human-readable validator contract.
Structured validation must distinguish valid pending journals from malformed pending journals with deterministic field-specific diagnostics and must not mutate canonical files.
Read-only validation and snapshot paths must never create the advisory lock file; they may lock only an existing lock without mutating the project.
Existing-lock-only read paths must tolerate lock replacement races without creating filesystem entries, and their advisory snapshot limitation must be explicit.
The disappearing-lock race is covered by a focused regression test that proves the read-only helper does not recreate the lock file.
Read-only snapshot failures use deterministic category messages rather than exception-specific text, keeping machine consumers stable across Python versions.
Structured validation errors must use stable category diagnostics rather than raw parser, OS, or exception text; malformed transaction shape messages remain field-specific.
Read-only snapshot and structured validation must contain lock-acquisition OSError/RuntimeError failures behind stable diagnostics instead of leaking host-specific exception text.
Read-only snapshots must contain malformed non-object state/event payload failures behind a stable validation diagnostic instead of leaking type-dependent exceptions.
Structured validation must reject non-object state payloads with a deterministic diagnostic before field access, preventing uncaught AttributeError and preserving non-mutating behavior.
